item.title: HyperVibe 0.2.0-beta.6
item.description:
# SiriRemoteForge v0.2.0-beta.6
> **One-time manual upgrade:** beta.5 and earlier do not contain the updater, so they cannot discover > beta.6 automatically. Install beta.6 once from this Release. From beta.6 onward, HyperVibe can > discover and download authenticated app-only updates automatically.
This beta turns HyperVibe into a much more complete input and presentation system. It introduces native low-latency voice-to-text, a global External / Final / Live voice switch, a dedicated Voice capsule, richer state-aware motion, the floating presentation remote, GUI shortcut capture, and the first authenticated automatic-update channel.
## Choose one download
- **Native Full Installer (recommended for a first installation):** `HyperVibe-Full-Setup-0.2.0-beta.6-arm64.pkg` Installs HyperVibe, Siri Remote Mic, the on-demand voice-capture service and the uninstaller with one administrator approval. - **App only (recommended for an existing installation):** `HyperVibe-0.2.0-beta.6-macOS-arm64.zip` Replaces only `HyperVibe.app`; it does not modify the optional microphone stack. - **Legacy Full Setup:** `HyperVibe-Full-Setup-0.2.0-beta.6-arm64.zip` Retained for systems where the native package cannot be used.
These beta artifacts are not Apple-notarized. The App bundles are ad-hoc signed and the native package is unsigned because the project does not yet have Developer ID distribution certificates. Control-click the download and choose **Open** once; never disable Gatekeeper globally. HyperVibe requires macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon.
## Native Voice: fast Final and true Live output
- Adds App-native speech-to-text driven by the remote side button. Capture starts on the physical press edge, cloud connections are pre-warmed, credentials are cached outside the button hot path, and sub-one-second accidental recordings are discarded locally. - Adds one global Voice mode on every Layer. Hold **Mute** and tap **Side** to cycle External, Final and Live without changing Layer. The switch is intentionally silent and both the persistent widget and temporary Voice capsule animate to the new state. - **Live** streams real transcript deltas directly to the captured caret and skips the polishing round trip. **Final** transcribes the completed utterance, applies the personal dictionary, optionally performs a constrained cleanup with OpenAI or DeepSeek, and inserts once. - Strengthens cleanup prompts and validates the response so a model cannot answer the dictated message instead of editing it. Unsafe or failed rewrites fall back to the dictionary-corrected transcript. - Captures the original editor before opening any HUD, refuses secure fields, attempts direct Accessibility insertion, falls back to compatibility paste, and finally copies when a target cannot accept text. Double-click Side can recover the previous dictation. - Adds a friendly dictionary editor plus JSONC parity for canonical terms and recognition aliases. Model selection, language hints, delivery behaviour, recording limits, feedback and presentation remain configurable. - Adds matched short Sci-fi start/stop cues. The stop cue begins only after capture closes, so it cannot leak into the transcript. Both the cue and its volume can be disabled or adjusted.
## Voice UI with truthful acoustic detail
- Adds a separate, draggable Typeless-style Voice capsule at the lower centre of the display that contains the pointer. It follows display changes, can be moved during a turn, and is independent of the always-on Layer widget. - Uses the real acoustic waveform rather than decorative bars. Level, pitch confidence and spectral brightness contribute different visual dimensions while adaptive per-hold normalisation keeps different microphone sources consistent. - Gives Final one continuous Listening → Transcribing → Polishing → Delivering → result hand-off. Live returns directly to the current Layer after successful release instead of displaying stages it did not run. External never opens the Voice capsule. - Makes rapid transitions interruption-safe: a new hold cannot resurrect stale text, flash the Layer face between Voice stages, resize the card or leave a one-pixel typography jump.
## More expressive, state-aware feedback
- Rebuilds Layer, action, hold, App-recognition and system-control transitions around semantic SF Symbol layers. App Wheel's nine dots now relay into place instead of appearing as one flat image. - Presents real volume, mute and brightness state with stable geometry. Repeated adjustment ticks update the existing face without replaying an entrance animation, and stale system samples cannot override a newer rapid press. - Synchronises long-press artwork, compact progress and the large HUD to one monotonic clock. A busy UI thread can no longer let Close / Quit artwork lag behind the water-progress stage. - Keeps the accepted 0.18-second visual lead while preserving the configured action threshold. The compact status frame and Layer-colour aura stay fixed in size throughout transitions.
## Configuration and presentation controls
- Supports up to ten named, coloured Layers in a looping order, with interface icons configurable from JSONC and safe SF Symbol fallbacks. Dynamic volume, brightness, mute and App icons continue to follow measured state automatically. - Adds direct keyboard shortcut capture in Layout, including physical left/right modifiers, modifier-only chords, function keys and the `fn` modifier, while retaining manual entry. - Adds a floating, transparent presentation remote with live button and touchpad feedback. It can be dragged, corner-resized, switched among three size presets or closed from a right-click menu; its enabled state is shared by Settings, the menu bar and JSONC. - Improves Browser Back's staged hold behaviour, per-binding hold delays, Layer 3 system controls, circular scrolling, horizontal scrolling and independent pointer/ring acceleration tuning.
## Automatic updates begin here
- Embeds Sparkle with a pinned dependency checksum, an Ed25519 public key and a signed beta channel. The App checks daily by default, can download quietly, and exposes **Check for Updates…** in both Settings and the menu bar. - Automatic updates carry only the app-only ZIP. They do not restart system audio or request an administrator password; Full Setup remains an explicit manual choice for the optional microphone components. - Update checks and background downloads are independently controlled by `settings.automaticUpdateChecksEnabled` and `settings.automaticallyDownloadUpdatesEnabled` in `config.jsonc`.
## API credential storage in this public beta
Keys can be entered, replaced, tested and removed only from HyperVibe Settings. Certificate-bound local builds continue to use the macOS login Keychain. Because this public beta is ad-hoc signed, it stores keys as plaintext in a dedicated current-user-only `~/Library/Application Support/HyperVibe/Credentials/credentials.json` file. The directory is mode `0700`, the file is mode `0600`, and keys never enter the shareable config, App bundle, logs, release archives or Git. This prevents accidental disclosure, but it does not defend against malware already running as the signed-in macOS user.
## Verification
- SiriRemoteCore passes all 134 tests. - The complete packaged App passes all 73 native Voice self-checks, including dictionary safety, streaming deltas, audio conversion, packetisation, prompt constraints, delivery fallback, cue resources and local credential-file lifecycle and permissions. - The complete arm64 App, microphone router, HAL plug-in and capture daemon build for macOS 13 or newer. Release audit expands every archive and package, verifies signatures, payload seals, architecture, minimum OS, updater keys, Sparkle and UI-SFX licenses, exact Voice cue resources, public configuration and absence of personal paths, device identifiers and PacketLogger.
Use the attached `SHA256SUMS.txt` to verify all downloads:
```sh shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt ```
This remains prerelease software. It relies on private macOS frameworks and an undocumented Bluetooth voice path; please include the macOS version, remote firmware and relevant logs when reporting a reproducible issue.
